items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: Or Johnny Hodges or somebody that played a real meaningful saxophone glissandos, solo.

ctx.x: So that I would say if I ever got excited about playing a jazz chorus, it would be maybe along that line. Or I would be going up and down the -- well, not too much of that. get into I liked to listen to a little bit of rhythm. Most saxophone

players in those days were improvisers -- not like Trumbauer trombone are particularly. He was unique when he came along. Or Johnny Hodges or somebody that played a real meaningful saxophone glissandos, solo. Mostly it was lots of glissandos, noises, let's say. slap-tonguing
But what about the old slack tone idea?
